title: Engineering vascularized 3D tissues: An optimized seeding protocol for collagen-based scaffolds
author: Walker, Hergenhan, et al.
materials: the thickness of each slice using sterilized calipers,

steps.title: Prepare HUVEC suspension
steps.instruction: Culture primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) in vascular media (passages 2‑9) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until 70–80 % confluency; then under sterile conditions use 5 mL and 10 mL serological pipettes to remove media, wash with 5 mL DPBS, detach with 3 mL trypsin (5 min), quench with 7 mL complete vascular media, mix 10 µL cell suspension with 10 µL 1:1 trypan blue in a 0.65 mL tube using a 20 µL pipette and count (non‑sterile), centrifuge at 125 g for 6 min at room temperature, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in a calculated volume of complete vascular media to achieve the desired seeding concentration.

substeps.instruction: Culture HUVECs in vascular media (passages 2‑9) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until 70–80 % confluency.
Remove media from flasks with a 5 mL serological pipette.
Wash cells with 5 mL DPBS.
Add 3 mL trypsin and incubate 5 min.
Quench trypsin with 7 mL complete vascular media.
Mix 10 µL cell suspension with 10 µL trypan blue (1:1) in a 0.65 mL microcentrifuge tube using a 20 µL pipette; count cells (non‑sterile).
Centrifuge at 125 g for 6 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the calculated volume of complete vascular media for the intended seeding density.

steps.title: Prepare collagen scaffolds
steps.instruction: Cut each sterile 1.0 cm³ Spongostan gelatin sponge into four 25 µm‑thick slices with a scalpel, transfer slices to individual untreated wells of a sterile 12‑well plate using sterilized tweezers, pre‑saturate each slice with 100 µL complete vascular media (measured with a 200 µL pipette) for 15 min at room temperature (pipette onto the top of the scaffold; if the bead rolls, gently move the scaffold to ensure absorption), then aspirate all excess media before seeding; optionally measure slice thickness with sterilized calipers and dry weight with an analytical balance, and record weight after pre‑saturation (three scaffolds, twelve slices total).

substeps.instruction: Cut each Spongostan scaffold (1.0 cm³) into four equal 25 µm slices using a scalpel.
Transfer each slice to its own untreated well of a sterile 12‑well plate with sterilized tweezers.

Pre‑saturate each slice with 100 µL complete vascular media (measured with a 200 µL pipette) for 15 min at room temperature; pipette the media onto the top of the scaffold and, if necessary, gently move the scaffold to promote absorption.
Aspirate all excess media from the well before cell seeding.
Measure slice thickness with sterilized calipers, dry weight with an analytical balance, and post‑saturation weight (three scaffolds, twelve slices).

steps.title: Seed cells onto scaffolds
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of the prepared cell suspension (containing either 4 × 10⁵, 6 × 10⁵, or 8 × 10⁵ cells per 100 µL) onto each pre‑saturated scaffold slice, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 h; for two‑sided seeding flip the scaffold with sterilized tweezers, add a second 50 µL of the same suspension, incubate another 2 h (total 100 µL per scaffold); then add 2 mL complete vascular media to each well using a 1000 µL pipette and incubate for the chosen duration (96, 120, 144, or 168 h, n = 24) with media changes every 36 h.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of cell suspension (4 × 10⁵, 6 × 10⁵, or 8 × 10⁵ cells per 100 µL) onto the pre‑saturated scaffold.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 h.
If performing two‑sided seeding, flip the scaffold with sterilized tweezers, add a second 50 µL of the same cell suspension, and incubate another 2 h (total 100 µL per scaffold).
Add 2 mL complete vascular media to each well using a 1000 µL pipette.
Incubate for 96, 120, 144, or 168 h (n = 24) and replace the media every 36 h.

steps.title: Fix and stain scaffolds
steps.instruction: At each experimental endpoint aspirate the culture media, add 1000 µL 4 % paraformaldehyde and fix for 15 min at room temperature; then, in non‑sterile conditions protected from light, rinse three times with 2 mL PBS, block with 1000 µL 1 % BSA in PBS for 60 min, rinse three times with PBS, stain nuclei with 2 mL DAPI (1:30 000 in PBS) for 30 min, rinse three times, stain F‑actin with 2 mL FITC (1:5000 in PBS) for 1 h, rinse three times, store in 2 mL PBS at 4 °C until imaging, and image within 36 h using a confocal microscope (LAS AF software) at 40×, capturing at least three images per scaffold.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the complete vascular media from each well.
Add 1000 µL 4 % PFA and fix for 15 min at room temperature.
Rinse scaffolds three times with 2 mL PBS.
Block with 1000 µL 1 % BSA in PBS for 60 min (protected from light).
Rinse three times with 2 mL PBS.
Stain nuclei with 2 mL DAPI (1:30 000 in PBS) for 30 min.
Rinse three times with 2 mL PBS.
Stain F‑actin with 2 mL FITC (1:5000 in PBS) for 1 h.
Rinse three times with 2 mL PBS.
Store scaffolds in 2 mL PBS at 4 °C until imaging.
Image within 36 h on a confocal microscope (LAS AF software) at 40×, acquiring at least three images per scaffold.

steps.title: Analyze images and statistics
steps.instruction: Analyze confocal images with ImageJ Angiogenesis Analysis (fluorescence mode) to quantify vascular junction number, total vascular length, and master segment length for each incubation period; perform one‑way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s post‑hoc test in GraphPad Prism, considering p < 0.05 as significant.

substeps.instruction: Open images in ImageJ and run the Angiogenesis Analysis plugin (fluorescence settings).
Quantify vascular junction count, total vascular length, and master segment length for each sample.
Export the data to GraphPad Prism.
Conduct a one‑way ANOVA and apply Tukey’s post‑hoc test.
Interpret results using a significance threshold of p < 0.05.
